title: S0/S2/G2: Definition must use the transfer system O nontrivially (no reduction to HHR)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Faithfulness gap (F1, definitional drift).** The problem demands a filtration *adapted to an incomplete transfer system* $\aO$. A solution that defines the generators/connectivity in a way that ignores $\aO$ and silently reproduces the Hill–Hopkins–Ravenel (complete) slice filtration answers the wrong question.

**To establish.**
- Specify *exactly* which slice cells / admissible norms / admissible $H$-sets enter the generating set, as an explicit function of the transfer system $\aO$ (equivalently its indexing system $\mathcal F^{\aO}_\bullet$).
- Make the dependence of the connectivity function $f_{\aO}(n,H)$ on $\aO$ explicit.
- **Boundary checks (mandatory):** at the *trivial* transfer system the construction must reduce to the Postnikov/Borel-type filtration; at the *complete* transfer system it must reduce to the HHR slice filtration. If either extreme is wrong, the definition is wrong.
- Note the first genuinely *incomplete* case occurs for $G$ with a nontrivial subgroup lattice (e.g. $C_{p^2}$, $C_{pq}$); $C_p$ has only the two extreme transfer systems.

Reference: Blumberg–Hill, *Operadic multiplications...norms and transfers*, Adv. Math. 2015 (indexing systems = transfer systems).

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Resolved.** I added a dedicated subsection "The dependence on $\aO$ is nontrivial: boundary checks and the first incomplete cases" (immediately after the connectivity-function/convention discussion), turning the previously informal remarks into proved statements that pin down the $\aO$-dependence end to end.

**What is now explicit.**
- *Generators as a function of $\aO$:* the generating cells of $\tau^\aO_{\ge n}$ are $G_+\otimes_H N^T S^1$ for $\aO$-admissible $T=\coprod_i H/K_i$, i.e. all stabilizers satisfy $K_i\to_\aO H$. This is verbatim the indexing system $\mathcal F^\aO_\bullet$.
- *Connectivity function:* $f_\aO(n,H)=\lceil n/r_H\rceil$ with $r_H=[H:\chi^\aO(H)]$, $\chi^\aO(H)=\min\{K\mid K\to_\aO H\}$. The admissible-index lemma shows $r_H$ is exactly the maximal cardinality of a single-orbit admissible $H$-set $H/\chi^\aO(H)$, linking generators and connectivity.
- *Monotonicity (new Prop):* $\aO\subseteq\aO'\Rightarrow \chi^{\aO'}(H)\subseteq\chi^\aO(H)$, $r^{\aO'}_H\ge r^\aO_H$, $f_{\aO'}\le f_\aO$, hence $\tau^{\aO'}_{\ge n}\subseteq\tau^\aO_{\ge n}$. So trivial = coarsest, complete = finest, every incomplete strictly between.

**Mandatory boundary checks (now Propositions with proof).**
- *Trivial $\aO$ = Postnikov:* $\chi^{\mathrm{triv}}(H)=H$, $r_H=1$, only trivial orbits admissible, generators reduce to $G/H_+\otimes S^k$, $f_{\mathrm{triv}}(n,H)=n$, criterion = $\mathrm{conn}(E^H)\ge n$ for all $H$.
- *Complete $\aO$ = HHR:* $\chi^{\mathrm{compl}}(H)=\{e\}$, $r_H=|H|$, free orbit $H/e$ gives $S^{\rho_H}$ and the cells $G_+\wedge_H S^{m\rho_H}$, $f_{\mathrm{compl}}(n,H)=\lceil n/|H|\rceil$ = Hill–Yarnall (HHR slice).

**First genuinely incomplete cases (new Proposition + remarks).**
- Noted $C_p$ has only the two extremes.
- Full table of all **five** transfer systems on $C_{p^2}$ (chain $e<C_p<G$, Cat(3)=5), with $\chi^\aO$ and $r_H$. The incomplete system $\{C_p\to G\}$ gives $r_G=p$ — strictly between $1$ (Postnikov) and $p^2=|G|$ (HHR) — so $f_\aO(n,G)=\lceil n/p\rceil$. Crucially the free orbit $G/e$ (card $p^2$) is **not** admissible there, so the HHR cell $S^{\rho_G}=N^{G/e}S^1$ is excluded, while $N^{G/C_p}S^1$ (card $p$, $\Phi^G$-value $S^1$) is the maximal admissible orbit. This shows the construction is not a reparametrization of HHR.
- $C_{pq}$ remark: the incomplete system $\{e\to C_p\}$ gives the asymmetric profile $r_{C_p}=p,\,r_{C_q}=1,\,r_G=1$ (HHR-like in one direction, Postnikov-like in the other), irreducible to any rescaling $n\mapsto n/|H|$.

All values verified numerically (transfer-system enumeration via transitivity + restriction-axiom closure; $\chi^\aO$, $r_H$, admissibility, and $\Phi^G N^T S^1\simeq S^{|T/G|}$). Table rules use `\hline` inside the math `array`; brace/environment balance checked. No LaTeX toolchain in sandbox, so compilation not run.
